titulo: Should you rinse raw chicken before cooking it?
fuentes: CDC: raw chicken doesn't need to be washed; cook to 165 °F; wash hands with soap and water
USDA FSIS / NC State study of 300 home cooks in test kitchens (J Food Prot 2022)

frases.texto: You rinse your raw chicken before cooking it.

frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: Water doesn't kill the bacteria. It can just spread them.
The CDC says rinsing can spread germs to your sink, your counter, and other food.
A USDA-backed study put about three hundred people in test kitchens.
Of those who washed their chicken, six in ten had bacteria in the sink afterward.
Cooking is what kills them: chicken needs to hit one hundred sixty-five degrees inside.
Heads up: wash your hands with soap and water after touching raw chicken.
Skip the rinse, cook it, done.
Send this to the friend who rinses chicken like they're giving it a bath.
